article.title: Uplift Modeling: Finding Customers Whose Behavior You Can Actually Change
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven decisions.

paragraphs.en: Traditional propensity modeling asks a useful question: who is most likely to produce an outcome such as purchasing, renewing, or responding? For many campaigns, however, the more valuable question is different: whose behavior will change because of the intervention? Uplift modeling, also called heterogeneous treatment-effect modeling in related contexts, tries to estimate that incremental difference. Consider two customers. Customer A has a 90 percent probability of purchasing even without a coupon. Customer B has a 40 percent probability without the coupon but a 65 percent probability if the coupon is sent. A propensity model may rank A above B, yet B offers much more incremental value. Targeting only the highest propensities can spend incentives on people who would have converted anyway. The causal quantity behind uplift is the difference between potential outcomes under treatment and control. For an individual, both outcomes can never be observed simultaneously, which is the fundamental problem of causal inference. Randomized experiments provide training data that help estimate average and heterogeneous treatment effects because treatment assignment is independent of pre-treatment characteristics in expectation. Several modeling strategies exist. Two-model approaches estimate outcomes separately for treated and control populations and subtract predictions. Meta-learners such as S-, T-, X-, and R-learners organize outcome and treatment-effect estimation in different ways. Tree-based causal forests and uplift trees seek subgroups with heterogeneous responses. The method is less important than the identification assumptions and evaluation design. A model can appear to find dramatic uplift if treatment assignment was confounded or if post-treatment variables leaked into features. Evaluation is also different from ordinary prediction. Because the true individual treatment effect is unobservable, standard accuracy cannot be calculated directly. Analysts may use uplift curves, Qini-style measures, policy value, or doubly robust evaluation on experimental or appropriately adjusted data. Business value should remain central. A positive treatment effect may still be unprofitable if the intervention is expensive. The optimal policy can depend on incremental margin, incentive cost, contact cost, capacity, and customer fatigue. Negative uplift is important too. Some customers may be harmed or discouraged by an intervention, suggesting that the best action is not to contact them. Calibration of treatment-effect estimates is challenging, so decisions should include uncertainty and validation across time. Segment stability matters because heterogeneous effects are often noisier than outcome predictions. Large samples are usually required, particularly when baseline conversion is rare. Uplift modeling also changes how campaign success is discussed. High conversion among contacted customers is not the objective by itself. The goal is additional outcomes caused by contact relative to what would have happened without it. This distinction connects model evaluation to experimental design. Control groups are not wasted customers; they provide the counterfactual information needed to learn incremental value. Organizations moving from propensity to uplift should resist treating uplift as simply a new score column. It requires reliable treatment logging, clear eligibility rules, randomized or credibly adjusted comparisons, and decision economics. When those foundations exist, uplift modeling can redirect resources from customers who are merely likely to act toward customers whose actions the business can actually influence. Analysts should define the population, observation window, and decision rule before interpreting the result. A useful review separates the observed pattern from the mechanism that may have produced it and from the action that should follow. paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整翻譯與解說：本文重點在於把 model metric 或 KPI 放回實際 decision context。數字變大不一定更好；極端群體可能自然回歸平均；ranking 與 probability calibration 是不同能力；歷史資料也會承載舊政策；而 campaign 真正關心的常常是 intervention 所創造的增量效果。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳・解説：model metricやKPIはdecision contextの中で解釈する必要がある。数値が大きいこと自体が良いとは限らず、極端群は平均へ回帰し、rankingとprobability calibrationは別の性能である。historical dataには旧policyも刻まれ、campaignではinterventionによる増分効果が重要になる。
